[NextItNet (WSDM 2019)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) already captures short- and long-range dependencies through residual causal convolutions with fixed dilation schedules. [SkipRec (AAAI 2021)](https://cdn.aaai.org/ojs/16518/16518-13-20012-1-2-20210518.pdf) adds sequence-dependent layer skipping to deep sequential recommenders, including NextItNet: close precedent for contextual computation selection, although not soft mixing across dilation branches. Outside recommendation, [ADCNN (Pattern Recognition 2022)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0031320321005495) makes dilation content-dependent. These precedents weaken broad novelty claims about adaptive receptive fields; this search did not establish an exact match for shared convolution kernels across dilations with input-dependent scalar mixing.

[AdaMCT (CIKM 2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2205.08776v3) provides particularly relevant gating evidence: pooled sequence representations generate personalized, layer-specific scalar coefficients mixing CNN and Transformer features. Table 3 compares adaptive fusion against several fixed coefficients; adaptive fusion performs better across three Amazon datasets. However, this concerns local/global module fusion, not shared-kernel dilation selection, and does not establish superiority over globally learned, input-independent mixing. For the proposed NextItNet variant, informative controlled ablations would compare uniform mixing, tuned fixed coefficients, globally learned coefficients, and contextual gates, holding dilation branches and kernel sharing constant. Expected gains remain uncertain.

AdaMCT evaluates against 100 sampled negatives. The pinned benchmark’s 99-negative HR@10 likewise measures candidate-set ranking rather than full-catalog top-10 retrieval. [Krichene and Rendle (KDD 2020)](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons relative to exact metrics, even in expectation. Small validation improvements therefore support only cautious, benchmark-specific conclusions; they do not independently demonstrate better full-catalog recommendations or successful short-/long-term interest separation.
